problem.title: Gracefulness of every tree having a path within distance two of every vertex
problem.informal_statement:
Decide whether every finite tree T that has a path subgraph P, possibly a single vertex, with every vertex of T within graph distance 2 of P admits a graceful labelling: a bijection from V(T) onto {0,...,m} whose induced absolute edge differences are exactly {1,...,m}, where m is the number of edges.

The class is frozen locally by that distance condition and by nothing else. It strictly contains the caterpillars, which are the distance-1 case and are classically graceful, and it is strictly contained in the class of all trees, so the target is a strict special case of the Graceful Tree Conjecture and never that conjecture. Extending an exhaustive verification frontier by one vertex count is a capability result and is not progress on this target. A bounded exhaustion is bounded evidence; one certified non-graceful member would refute the target.

target_claim.statement: For every integer m >= 0 and every finite simple tree T with exactly m edges such that there exists a path subgraph P of T with at least one vertex and every vertex of T within graph distance 2 of some vertex of P, there exists a bijection phi from V(T) onto {0,1,...,m} whose induced edge labelling psi(uv) = abs(phi(u) - phi(v)) satisfies the set equality {psi(e) : e in E(T)} = {1,2,...,m}.

assumption_claims.statement: A tree is a finite simple connected acyclic undirected graph with at least one vertex. For a tree T, m = card(E(T)) and card(V(T)) = m + 1. Distance d_T(u,v) is the number of edges on the unique T-path from u to v, and d_T(v,v) = 0. Infinite trees, forests, multigraphs, and rooted, plane, or edge-weighted trees are outside the definition.

A graceful labelling of a tree T with m edges is a bijection phi from V(T) onto {0,1,...,m} such that {abs(phi(u) - phi(v)) : uv in E(T)} = {1,2,...,m} as sets; since card(E(T)) = m this is equivalent to the induced edge labelling being a bijection onto {1,...,m}. T is graceful iff at least one such phi exists. Rejected readings: vertex labels drawn from {1,...,m+1}; edge labels merely injective without covering {1,...,m}; signed or modular differences; an alpha-labelling, which additionally requires a boundary value separating the bipartition classes and is strictly stronger; k-graceful and near-graceful variants that shift the edge-label range.

A tree T belongs to the frozen class X iff there exists a subgraph P of T isomorphic to a path on k >= 1 vertices, so a single vertex and no edges is allowed, such that every v in V(T) satisfies d_T(v,w) <= 2 for some w in V(P). P is called a spine and need not be unique, longest, or diametral. Rejected readings: deleting every leaf of T yields a caterpillar, which agrees for large trees but is degenerate for the one-vertex and one-edge trees where the leaf-deleted graph is empty; diameter at most 5; and the formally stronger requirement that some longest path of T meet every vertex within distance 2, whose equivalence to the frozen condition is unproved here and is not assumed.

A caterpillar is the distance-1 case of the frozen class definition: some path subgraph P has every vertex of T within distance 1 of V(P). Caterpillars therefore form a subclass of X, and the containment is strict with an exactly checkable witness: the seven-vertex tree obtained from K_{1,3} by subdividing every edge once lies in X, taking the spine through two legs and the centre, but deleting its leaves leaves K_{1,3}, which is not a path, so it is not a caterpillar. The class X is also strictly contained in the class of all trees, witnessed by the tree obtained from K_{1,3} by subdividing every edge twice.

Every quantity on the trust path is an exact arbitrary-precision integer or an exact finite set of such integers. Permitted operations are integer subtraction, absolute value, integer comparison, set and multiset equality, and byte comparison of canonical-form strings. No floating-point value, tolerance, statistical estimate, or heuristic score may appear in a certificate or in any verifier decision; such output is exploration-only and is labelled as such. Tree counts used in coverage checks are recomputed from an exact integer recurrence inside the run and are never taken from a table, a published figure, or recollection.

In a tree, any two vertices are joined by exactly one path, so graph distance is well defined, and deleting all leaves of a finite tree with at least two vertices yields a tree or the empty graph. Iterating leaf deletion terminates in a single vertex or a single edge, which defines the centroid or bicentroid used by the canonical form.

Every caterpillar is graceful. This is treated as a standard textbook fact about graceful labellings and is the reason the caterpillar class is excluded from being the frozen target. Its usual attribution and date are a separate untrusted claim and are not used.

If phi is a graceful labelling of a tree with m edges then the map v -> m - phi(v) is also a graceful labelling, since it is a bijection onto {0,...,m} and preserves every absolute difference. This symmetry may halve a labelling search by fixing one orientation; it never justifies skipping a tree.

The operator notes, by way of the planning dossier, report exhaustive verification of the Graceful Tree Conjecture through 35 vertices as of July 2026. Untrusted and additionally ambiguous: it is not recorded whether 35 counts vertices or edges, whether all trees or a subclass were covered, whether labellings were retained as certificates, or whether the computation has been independently replayed. The exact source is unidentified. The ADR-0055 pre-research novelty re-check must cover this claim.

That the gracefulness of the frozen class X is not settled is the load-bearing status claim of this dossier and is untrusted. It rests on the common attribution of an open conjecture about lobsters to Bermond in 1979 and on the absence of a known classical theorem of the caterpillar type covering X. Neither has been checked against an acquired source. If X turns out to be settled, the correct outcome is a superseding record rather than a re-scoped target. The ADR-0055 re-check must cover this claim first.

Members of the frozen class that admit a perfect matching are reported, from recollection and without an acquired source, to be graceful. Untrusted, and important: if true it covers a large proper part of X, so certificates produced there would be correct and worthless. The re-check must name this subcase explicitly, and any fitted labelling scheme must report whether it only covers that part.

That the frozen class X is what the literature calls the class of lobsters is a terminology claim and is untrusted. The name is used nowhere in the target claim, because published definitions differ on the degenerate one-vertex and one-edge cases. An acquired source's status statement may be transferred to this target only after its definition has been mapped row by row against the frozen class definition.

Extending an exhaustive verification frontier by one vertex count is a capability result and must never be recorded as progress on the frozen target; the planning dossier says so explicitly. A bounded exhaustion supports only the statement that every member of X inside the measured envelope is graceful, each with a replayed certificate, and never the universal claim.

A backtracking search for graceful labellings is easy to make incomplete by an unjustified pruning rule, and an incomplete search reports a non-graceful tree, which would be a refutation of the Graceful Tree Conjecture. Do not repeat that route blind: every pruning rule needs a stated soundness lemma, the pruned search must be cross-checked against unpruned enumeration for m <= 12, and a not-graceful verdict requires a second methodologically independent exhaustion whose proof log a checker replays.

formalization.statement: forall m : N, forall T : Tree, (InClassX(T) and edge_count(T) = m) -> exists phi : V(T) -> {0..m}, Bijective(phi) and { abs(phi(u) - phi(v)) : (u,v) in E(T) } = {1..m}, where InClassX(T) <-> exists P a path subgraph of T with at least one vertex, forall v in V(T), exists w in V(P), d_T(v,w) <= 2
quantifiers: forall m an integer with m >= 0
forall T a finite simple tree with exactly m edges and m + 1 vertices
exists P a path subgraph of T with at least one vertex, inside the hypothesis InClassX(T)
forall v in V(T), exists w in V(P) with d_T(v,w) <= 2, inside the hypothesis InClassX(T)
exists phi a bijection from V(T) onto {0,...,m}
forall e in E(T) the induced label abs(phi(u) - phi(v)) lies in {1,...,m}, and forall j in {1,...,m} some edge induces j

quantifier_mapping: non-negative integer edge count, unchanged from the source statement
narrowed from every tree to every tree in the frozen class X
existential labelling, unchanged from the source statement
new existential inside the hypothesis only: the spine witnessing membership in X
definition_mapping: phi bijective from V(T) onto the exact integer range {0,...,m}
absolute differences across its edges are exactly {1,...,m}
set equality of the induced edge labels abs(phi(u) - phi(v)) with {1,...,m}
finite simple connected acyclic graph with exactly m edges and m + 1 vertices
no counterpart in the source statement; a restriction introduced by this dossier
assumption_delta: The frozen target adds the hypothesis that T lies in the frozen class X and adds nothing else.
It removes no hypothesis of the source statement.
No matching, diameter, parity, or vertex-count hypothesis is imposed.
No claim is made that X is maximal for provability by any particular method.
edge_case_delta: m = 0, the one-vertex tree, is inside the claim: the unique labelling induces the empty edge-label set, which equals the empty range {1,...,0}.
m = 1, the single edge, is inside the claim, and the class definition admits it because a spine may be a single vertex.
The rejected leaf-deletion reading of the class definition is degenerate exactly on those two cases, which is why the distance form was frozen.
No closure property of X under reduction is assumed; a reduction rule is not presumed to keep a tree inside X.

success_criteria: an exact non-graceful member of the frozen class, certified under shape S4 including its independent second exhaustion
a proof that every member of the frozen class is graceful, with every lemma discharged symbolically rather than by table
a proved reduction rule that maps a member of the frozen class to a strictly smaller member and preserves gracefulness
an explicit unresolved outcome that names the smallest remaining obligation, together with the retained exclusion set and every refuted route
stopping_rules: stop on an exact certificate of either direction and open no further search
stop when fresh model spend reaches USD 20
stop when two consecutive review points close no proof obligation and refute no route
stop when retained class members exceed 5 * 10^6 or cumulative search nodes exceed 10^11
never promote a bounded exhaustion to the universal claim; a frontier extension is recorded as a capability result and not as progress on the target
